title: Learned Mirror phase contexts for parameter-superposed task models
hypothesis: For four independently learned task classifiers compressed into one shared parameter vector, a one-angle-per-task Mirror rotation context optimized on training examples will improve mean held-out task accuracy by at least 0.03 over fixed random-sign Parameter Superposition (PSP), while using no more serialized bytes than PSP and remaining within 0.05 mean accuracy of independent models.
physical_object: one shared 32-dimensional vector containing the sum of four context-bound task-model vectors
mirror_coordinate: one learned FP16 scalar angle per task; the view rotates adjacent weight pairs before binding and inverse-rotates after unbinding
logical_multiplicity: four task-specific classifiers reconstructed from one shared parameter vector

model.world: four independently seeded Gaussian linear teachers; train/test inputs are independent standard normal samples

controls: independent separately trained model per task (upper reference)
one shared tied classifier jointly trained on all tasks (hard-sharing control)
fixed random-sign PSP contexts, applied by elementwise binding and unbinding
fixed seeded random Mirror phase context
learned dense diagonal binding coefficients (simple higher-byte native control)

evaluation.primary_metric: macro mean and per-task held-out classification accuracy
evaluation.interference_metric: each compressed task model accuracy loss versus its independent model
evaluation.serialized_payload: actual ZIP/NPY FP16 inference payload bytes, including all context codes, shared tensor, metadata and reconstruction state
evaluation.active_compute: report coordinate-generation and bind/unbind arithmetic count; training examples, updates and wall clock

development_gate_before_fresh: On both development worlds, learned Mirror mean accuracy must be >= fixed-sign PSP +0.03, no more than 0.05 below independent mean accuracy, and actual payload bytes <= fixed-sign PSP. Otherwise fresh remains unopened.
success_gate: All three fresh worlds meet the frozen accuracy, interference and byte gates; report per-task quality and actual bytes.
failure_gate: Any development world misses a registered gate; fresh remains sealed.

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP16 inference payload after reload
paid_objects: any private task weights or reconstruction state

boundaries: linear synthetic task bank; not neural-network benchmark evidence
independent task models are trained before compression, so this measures retrieval/compression, not joint learning efficiency
task identities are held out by complete world seed in fresh evaluation
fixed random codes and all generated reconstruction state must be reproducible from paid metadata
